about: The commands of the : line and of a key bound to one (spec 0020), as people read them, for every front end: the line each front end lists (summary, and the words it takes), the longer text of docs/commands.md (doc; the page is made from this file by scripts/commands-doc.mjs), and the version that brought each in (since: "unreleased" until the bump, when scripts/version.mjs sync writes the version; a release refuses one left). A front end lists only what its own version has. The engine keeps only what reading a line needs (tc_core::keymap::COMMANDS: name, shortest form, the actions it runs, the words it takes); a test keeps the names, short forms and whether each takes words the same. Every action but the : itself has a command (spec 0025).

commands.name: tabnext
commands.summary: the next page, or a page by its number or name
commands.doc: With nothing after it, the next page, from the last back to the first. With a number, the page at that place in the top bar (1 to 9, Settings last; in the terminal app Kanban is 8, Console 9 and Settings 0); with a word, the first page whose name starts with it, in any case: `:tabn 3`, `:tabn tasks`, `:tabn bu`. The keys `gt` and `g1` to `g9` (and `g0` in the terminal app) run it.

commands.name: tabprevious
commands.doc: The page before this one, from the first round to the last. `gT` runs it.

commands.name: tabNext
commands.doc: The same as `:tabprevious`, as in vim.

commands.name: tabfirst
commands.doc: The first page of the top bar, Tasks.

commands.name: tabrewind
commands.doc: The same as `:tabfirst`, as in vim.

commands.name: tablast
commands.doc: The last page of the top bar, Settings.

commands.name: quit
commands.doc: Quit the terminal app. The web app and the phone have nothing to quit.

commands.name: undo
commands.doc: Taskwarrior's `undo`, which asks first: on the terminal in a box, on the web with the line put on the command line for Enter.

commands.name: write
commands.doc: Sync, as vim's `:w` writes what has changed: on the terminal `task sync` in the background, with Taskwarrior's own settings; on the web and the phone, with the store. The same as `:sync`.

commands.name: edit
commands.doc: Read the report and the settings again, as vim's `:e` reads the file again. The terminal app reads `settings.json` again too, so a change made in an editor applies. `:edit settings` opens `settings.json` in `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR`, on the terminal.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: every key and command, and what each does
commands.doc: The list of keys and commands, as `?` opens it.

commands.name: filter
commands.summary: the Tasks page with a filter
commands.doc: With words, the Tasks page with them as its filter, as `task` reads a filter: `:filter +home due.before:eow`. With none, the cursor in the filter, to change it. Bound to a key, it is a saved filter a key away: `"tasks": { "g h": "filter +home" }`. On a page with a filter of its own (the web app's other pages), the cursor goes to that one.

commands.name: sort
commands.takes: fields with +, -, --, = or / after them; or replace and a whole sort
commands.doc: On the terminal. Each word changes the sort in place, in order: `due+` sorts by due ascending (added last when it is not a key yet), `due-` descending, `due--` takes it out, `due=` turns its direction round, and `due/` groups by it, or stops (`due+/` does both). `:sort due- project--` changes two keys and leaves the rest. `:sort replace due+,urgency-` sets the whole sort, as `report.<name>.sort` writes it. With none, the sort editor; in it, `:sort +` adds a key, and `--`, `=` and `/` do theirs to the key under the cursor, and `raise`, `lower`, `reset`, `apply` and `cancel` the editor's own steps.

commands.name: delete
commands.summary: delete the task, or the marked ones
commands.doc: Delete the chosen task, or the marked tasks when there are any. Taskwarrior asks first. `:delete completed` deletes the completed tasks of the report.

commands.name: mark
commands.summary: mark the task, or unmark it, and move down
commands.doc: Mark the chosen task, or unmark it, and move to the next row. With tasks marked, the task commands act on all of them. `:mark all` marks every row (or unmarks them all when they are all marked); `:mark range` every row from the last one marked to this one.

commands.name: open
commands.summary: open the task's link, or what is under the cursor
commands.doc: Open the first link in the chosen task, in its description and then its annotations: on the web in a new tab, on the terminal with the desktop's opener (`open`, or `xdg-open`). The terminal app looks at the task as it draws it, with your transformations applied, and in its string UDAs after the annotations, so a `FUL-3586` a rule makes a link opens it. On a list of projects or tags, of boards or kanbans, or of the kanbans in Settings, it opens the one under the cursor; on another row of Settings it uses it, as `Enter` does.

commands.name: done
commands.doc: Mark the chosen task done, or the marked tasks when there are any.

commands.name: start
commands.summary: start the task, or the marked ones not started
commands.doc: Start the chosen task. With tasks marked, start those not started yet and pass over the others.

commands.name: stop
commands.summary: stop the task, or the marked ones started
commands.doc: Stop the chosen task. With tasks marked, stop those started and pass over the others.

commands.name: toggle
commands.summary: start the task, or stop it when it is started
commands.doc: Start the chosen task, or stop it when it is started, as `+` does. With tasks marked, use `:start` or `:stop`.

commands.name: modify
commands.summary: modify the task, or the marked ones
commands.doc: With words, `task modify` with them on the marked tasks, or else on the chosen one: `:modify due:eow +next`. With none, the full form.

commands.name: annotate
commands.summary: annotate the task, or the marked ones
commands.doc: With words, add them as a note to the marked tasks, or else to the chosen one: `:annotate called back`. With none, a box for the note.

commands.name: denotate
commands.summary: take a note off the task
commands.takes: the note, or the start of it
commands.doc: With words, take off the note that starts with them, as `task denotate` does. With none, the command line with the task and `denotate` typed, for the note.

commands.name: duplicate
commands.doc: Taskwarrior's `duplicate` on the chosen task, or the marked ones.

commands.name: info
commands.takes: a tab: details, recurrence, timelog, annotations, unknown or raw; or modify or links
commands.doc: The chosen task's info: everything about it, its notes and how its urgency adds up. In the info, a tab by its name: `:info timelog`; `:info raw` is `task info` as `task` prints it. In the terminal, `:info modify` changes the task in the full form, as `m` does there (and as on the Tasks page `D` marks it done, `s` starts or stops it, `A` annotates it and `x` takes an annotation off), and `:info links` (`o` there) lists its links and the tasks it depends on and blocks, to open one. On a kanban in the terminal, the info of the card under the cursor.

commands.name: add
commands.takes: the task, as task add takes it
commands.doc: With words, add the task they describe, as `task add` reads them: `:add Buy milk +errand due:tomorrow`. With none, the box to add one, with a preview. It works from any page.

commands.name: report
commands.doc: With a name, the Tasks page with that report: `:report list`. With none, the list of reports to choose from. In the terminal's list of reports down the side, the report under the cursor. On a kanban, the report it is shown with here, without changing the saved kanban.

commands.name: context
commands.doc: With a name, Taskwarrior's `context` with it: `:context work`, or `:context none` to have none. With nothing after it, the list of contexts to choose from.

commands.name: sync
commands.doc: The same as `:write`.

commands.name: review
commands.summary: review the tasks that need it
commands.doc: tasksh's review: each task the `_reviewed` report lists, one at a time, to mark reviewed, skip, change or finish.

commands.name: lock
commands.summary: lock the app: with the PIN where there is one, else with the encryption secret
commands.doc: In the static web app. With nothing after it, the PIN screen on a trusted device with a PIN, in every tab, and the four keys of the PIN take it down; on any other device the full lock, as the lock button does, and the encryption secret or a passkey opens it again. `:lock pin` asks for the PIN screen (and says so where there is no PIN), `:lock key` for the full lock. Elsewhere (the web app on a Worker, the terminal) it says there is nothing to lock.

commands.name: next
commands.summary: the next month, the next board, the next column
commands.doc: On the calendar, the month after; on a board, the board after; on a kanban in the terminal, the column after. Like the other commands that act in several places, it does what it means on the page it is used on.

commands.name: previous
commands.summary: the month before, the board before, the column before
commands.doc: On the calendar, the month before; on a board, the board before; on a kanban in the terminal, the column before.

commands.name: snext
commands.doc: The next section of the settings, of a board, of the help or of a task's info, as vim's `:snext` is the next file in a split.

commands.name: sprevious
commands.doc: The section before, as `:snext` goes on.

commands.name: pagedown
commands.doc: A page down the list. A count is that many pages.

commands.name: pageup
commands.doc: A page up the list.

commands.name: halfdown
commands.doc: Half a page down the list, as `ctrl+d` does.

commands.name: halfup
commands.doc: Half a page up the list, as `ctrl+u` does.

commands.name: prompt
commands.doc: Put the cursor in the prompt, the command line at the bottom, as `/` does.

commands.name: sidebar
commands.summary: between the page and the reports down the side
commands.doc: On the terminal, move between the page and the list of reports down the side.

commands.name: hidden
commands.doc: In the terminal's list of reports, show the hidden ones too (their names start with `_`), or hide them again.

commands.name: back
commands.doc: Back to the page from the reports down the side, from a board to the list of boards, or from a kanban to the list of kanbans.

commands.name: stopall
commands.doc: Stop the task that is started, whichever it is (the timer in the top bar), where `:stop` stops the chosen one.

commands.name: reminders
commands.doc: The reminder options, and turning reminders on or off.

commands.name: export
commands.doc: Export the report as a file (JSON, CSV or TSV, with the fields you choose); on a board, a table of the board.

commands.name: clear
commands.doc: Clear what the console shows.

commands.name: burndown
commands.summary: the burndown by day, week or month
commands.doc: The burndown chart by day, by week or by month: `:burndown week`.

commands.name: command
commands.summary: run one of your task commands on the task
commands.doc: With nothing after it, one of your task commands to run on the chosen task, from a list. In the task commands of Settings, `:command add`, `:command edit` and `:command delete` add one, change the one under the cursor and delete it.

commands.name: key
commands.summary: add, take out or search keys
commands.takes: add, remove, none, defaults or search
commands.doc: In the Keybindings of Settings: `:key add` adds a key to the section, `:key remove` takes your key out (back to the default), `:key none` leaves the action without a key, `:key defaults` shows the default keys or only yours, `:key search` searches them.

commands.name: home
commands.summary: choose the page the app opens on
commands.doc: In the general settings, choose the page the app opens on: a report, a board or a kanban.

commands.name: apply
commands.doc: In Settings, apply the edits made on the page shown: what it changed is written into settings.json as the file is now. The terminal app's `Ctrl+S`; the web and the phone have an Apply button.

commands.name: revert
commands.doc: In Settings, drop the edits made on the page shown, back to what settings.json has.

commands.name: rule
commands.summary: add or delete a field transformation
commands.doc: In the appearance settings: `:rule add` adds a field transformation in a form, `:rule delete` deletes the one chosen.

commands.name: syncwhen
commands.doc: In the sync settings, choose when to sync.

commands.name: theme
commands.doc: In the appearance settings, choose the preset: auto, light, dark or mono.

commands.name: shading
commands.summary: the grey shading of tasks, or none
commands.doc: In the appearance settings, draw tasks' grey shading, or leave it out.

commands.name: kanban
commands.summary: the Kanban page, or a kanban's settings
commands.takes: since, other, new, column, edit, delete, raise, lower, write or off
commands.doc: With nothing after it, the Kanban page (in the terminal, where Kanban is on). On a kanban, `:kanban since` changes Completed since there and `:kanban other` shows or hides Other, the tasks no column has, and `:kanban fold` folds or unfolds the swimlane of the card under the cursor. In the Kanban section of the terminal's Settings: `:kanban new` adds a kanban, `:kanban column` a column, `:kanban edit` and `:kanban delete` change and delete what is under the cursor (while Kanban is off, `:kanban edit` sets it up the way under the cursor, Automatic or Manual), `:kanban raise` and `:kanban lower` move a column, `:kanban write` writes the `progressState` UDA and `:kanban off` turns Kanban off. See [Kanban](using/kanban.md).

commands.name: move
commands.summary: move the card to another column
commands.doc: On a kanban in the terminal, the card under the cursor to a column chosen from a list, running that column's On move on the task; `:move left` and `:move right` to the column beside it.

lines.summary: a row by its number, the last row
lines.doc: A number alone goes to that row of the list, as in vim; `:$` goes to the last. A count before `G` or `gg` does the same (`5G`).
A number with `+` or `-` moves that many rows down or up, as `3j` and `3k` do.
